summary: Check Point Software President Rupal Shah Hollenbeck says cybersecurity demand is rising and that 2024 could be 'a really fantastic year', even as rivals Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet report weak billings outlooks or face downgrades. The note covers Check Point's recent financials, acquisitions and new products, and Hollenbeck's comments on women in tech leadership. It also notes the impact of the war on the Tel Aviv-based company, whose operations she says continue normally.
one_line: Check Point's president predicts a fantastic 2024 amid growing cyber demand, while rivals Palo Alto and Fortinet cite macro uncertainty and weak billings outlooks.
key_facts: Cybercrime damage is projected to reach $10.5 trillion by 2025, which would rank third behind only the U.S. and China as a global economy.
Cybersecurity Ventures expects global cybercrime damage costs to increase 15% annually over the next two years.
Check Point's most recent quarter had non-GAAP EPS of $2.07, beating estimates by 5 cents, and revenue of $596.3M, beating by $3.78M.
Piper Sandler upgraded Check Point late last month, citing signs of recovery on the horizon.
Palo Alto Networks lowered its fiscal-year billings forecast, citing the cost of money and variability from financing and contract duration, but still sees demand.
Fortinet received a slew of analyst downgrades earlier this month over a disappointing fourth-quarter outlook; Cantor Fitzgerald called the near- to medium-term uncertain.
Check Point has made three recent acquisitions and launched products including the Rugged Industrial Control Systems Gateway and Playblocks.
Check Point increased headcount over the past year, including a 25% rise in its salesforce, and ended the quarter with $3B in cash.
Rupal Shah Hollenbeck has led Check Point for almost two years and spent more than two decades at Intel, then time at Oracle.
Nearly 17% of tech companies have a woman CEO, according to AnitaB.org; four of Check Point's top executives are women and three women sit on its board.
McKinsey data cited shows companies that improved women's representation outperformed their industry from 2019 to 2022.
Check Point is Tel Aviv-based; some employees have been killed in the war and others called to serve, but Hollenbeck says operations are normal.
Check Point's supply chain is 100% outside of Israel, with tech support and data centers around the world.
